question: In March 2023, the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) concluded a review of Euroins Romania. The preparatory steps taken by EIOPA to prepare this report were not disclosed to Euroins Romania or to its parent company, the Euroins Insurance Group. Neither company was invited to submit data to EIOPA. Moreover, EIOPA made no contact with the accounting and actuarial teams of either company.

The EIOPA report has not been made available to Parliament, making it impossible for Parliament to make an informed assessment of its accuracy or of the actuarial analysis that informed its findings. Will the Commission ask EIOPA to: 1.

immediately provide the sources of all data used in the report and indicate whether it made all the background reasoning for its assessment available to the company and the group’s supervisor (i.e. the Bulgarian regulator);
indicate the parties involved in any actuarial assessments made in the report’s preparation; and
explain why the actuarial teams from Euroins were not consulted?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.4.2024) The Commission understands that the report by the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA), which the Honourable Member refers to, was adopted pursuant to Article 8(1), point (b) of Regulation (EU) No 1094/2010 (EIOPA Regulation)1 with a view to assessing the correct and consistent application of the Solvency II framework2.

For this reason, the report was shared with both the Romanian and the Bulgarian supervisory authorities3. This report, which contains confidential prudential information, has not been made public, nor has it been shared with the Commission. The Honourable Member may, however, wish to submit a request for access to documents to EIOPA directly.

In addition, pursuant to Article 3 of the EIOPA Regulation4, the Chairperson of EIOPA may be requested to hold confidential oral discussions with relevant participants of the competent committee of the European Parliament. The Commission has not received any evidence of irregularities related to the preparation or content of EIOPA’s report.
Finally, the Commission understands that the Euroins Insurance Group is currently challenging EIOPA’s report at the Court of Justice of the European Union (see cases T416/23 and T-586/23).
